18: Nadezhda burst out laughing, put the book aside, and taking hold of Misha's shoulders, pulled him to her. He gave a squeal and threw himself into her arms exclaiming: "Pavloushka's bride!"
17: "Did I put you on your knees?" said Nadezhda in a voice of assumed indifference. "Why do you bother me?" "I'll not get up until you've forgiven me."
16: "Well, I've been punished, let me go, please," entreated Misha.
15: "I'm not keeping you there, you put yourself there," answered Nadezhda, smiling over her book.
14: "Well, I'm tired now," he said plaintively.
13: "Well, I'd better kneel here," said Misha.
11: "Who saved whom? You heard how they were talking of giving you a birching. Now go into the corner."
9: "You ought to let me off," said Misha. "I saved you from that bridegroom, so you ought to be grateful."
8: "All the same," she said, "you ought to go in the corner for listening."
6: "But you have forgotten that you oughtn't to listen behind doors."
4: And they began zealously to taunt one another and to argue as if they were discussing some important business matter.
